value.assumption_check: THREE, each measured or named. (1) That codemother's reply is posted before the tester's post() returns (shim.py:343 'post() pokes this shim directly at post time'; shim.py:645 posts the reply inside the handler) — the tooth under the fixture bus is what proves it, and if the reply is async the tester reads once more after flush, still inside the exchange. (2) That the tester's discard is a bus op (record_delivery) and not a delete of rows — the bus's own delivery mark is what undelivered() reads (bus.py:429); nothing is deleted. (3) That press_office has no other owner today — measured: it is a folder (~/.cairn/folders/press_office), no class-space device, no charter; only the instanceizer charter names it, as a tenant.
value.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs, and the ticket answers: WHERE does the tester post its seal exchange? The client path in cairn/devices/tester (grep 'post(' in device.py/cli.py — D1 names the function at build after measuring it). WHAT does it read back? bus.read(to='tester', channel='personal') filtered by reply_to == the envelope id it posted. WHAT does it print? one line per seal: 'crossed <proof>' or 'refused <proof>: <reason>' from the reply body's crossed[]/refused[]. HOW does it discard? bus.record_delivery(envelope id) for every personal envelope to 'tester' — measure the bus's delivery-mark method name first (bus.py near :429). WHERE is the one-time drain? a scratchpad script, not repo code; the count goes on the verdict artifact. WHICH charter changes? cairn/devices/cairn/intention+why.json owns[] += '~/.cairn/folders/press_office' via artifact.write(verb='charter'), recompile_gate.sh poked in the same act. WHY did one press_office envelope stand undelivered? diagnose at build in bus.py:208-240 _try_folder_delivery (the cached None at :225 after one failed load never retries — the first hypothesis); fix there, one tooth. WHAT NOT to touch: shim.py:645 (the reply is right), the bus schema, codemother's verb handlers.
value.collision_check: Over the whys. Law 6: press_office's ownership lands in the cairn device's charter via the artifact door's charter verb — the owner's gate; a folder has no charter to change. Tester charter (10) no live instance-space writes from run_proof — the discard marks delivery in the bus store, writes no file. one-web-server / no-daemons memory: no pulse is added to the tester; the reply is taken in the exchange. The operator inbox's read_email() (inbox.py:513) counts undelivered live — it keeps working and reads 0 for the tester after the build. No exclusive-and-terminal collision.
value.falsifier_check: DONE when (1) a proof tooth under a fixture bus: the tester posts a seal exchange, codemother's shim replies, and afterwards undelivered(to='tester') is EMPTY and the tester's own record_delivery shows it took the reply (crossed/refused per seal printed) — the tester did the clearing, not the proof; (2) a reply carrying refused[] is printed by the tester at the exchange, never silently stored; (3) the tester discards by default: after a fixture exchange no file under the tester's data_recorder inbound grows unless the tester chose to keep it (a keep is a named choice in code, not the default); (4) the cairn device's charter names ~/.cairn/folders/press_office among what it owns (a folder not owned by another device), through the charter verb of the artifact door, and a tooth shows a press_office-addressed envelope — the WATCHME kind included — lands in the folder recorder through the bus; (5) the standing pile is drained once by a hand (bus store is instance-space) and the count is on the verdict; afterwards a full tester run (cairn test) leaves undelivered(to='tester') at 0. RED if the tester's reply-taking needs a poll, a daemon, or a second process; RED if anything but the tester clears tester mail after the build. WRONG INTENT if Akien wants tester mail kept by default (his words say thrown away).
value.missing_check: ONE point not wrapped, on purpose and by his words: 'watch for a specific email as part of a test' — 'a long time from now'; recorded as a named IOU in the ticket (D6), not built. The activation of press_office's recorder from the email was measured BUILT (bus.py:208, 167 records) — so D4 records the ownership and fixes the one dropped envelope kind rather than building an activator. Everything else is a decision line.

value.better_approach: Considered wiring TesterShim into the tester process so replies deliver by poke. That makes the tester a shim-holding device with a pulse, and the tester is a subprocess notary that runs and exits — a client. Taking the reply inside the exchange it opened is smaller and needs no pulse. Considered having codemother stop replying to the tester: that silences refused[] for everyone; the reply is right, the taking was missing.
value.hidden_assumption: That the reply arrives within the exchange (codemother's shim handles the verb synchronously at post time — shim.py:343 says post() pokes the shim directly, so the reply is posted before the tester's post() returns). If codemother is not running, there is no reply to take and the seal exchange is already refused for want of a recipient; the tester prints that and discards nothing.
value.prior_art: cairn/tools/base/external.py:59 already reads undelivered(to=device_id) for external clients; shim.py:481 already reads the personal channel for the pane. The tester composes the same reads. the folder recorder already exists and the bus already activates it from the email (bus.py:208, instanceizer tenant since 2026-09-03) — his 'i'd bet you never built anything to activate it' is measured: it was built; one envelope kind slips. Congruency lab: no standing intention names who owns the press_office folder; the instanceizer charter names it as first tenant.
value.real_collision: Law 6 vs 'cairn owns press_office': a folder has no charter of its own; Akien's words give it an owner, recorded in the cairn device's charter through the door — the owner's gate, not an ambient transfer. Tester charter falsifier (10) 'a proof run through run_proof leaves no file in LIVE instance-space' — the tester's discard writes nothing; record_delivery is the bus's own store. No exclusive-and-terminal collision.
